title: Carry a delivered contribution to the fork
goal: When a contribution has been delivered, carry the same content to the fork and open a pull request there, so the fork holds the change and its checks have run.
success_condition: The bound verifier confirms, from the forge rather than from the worker, that an open pull request exists on the fork for this branch and that its checks have reached a resolved state with no check still in flight.

trigger.predicate: A contribution has been delivered that the fork does not yet carry, identified by the fork branch that would carry it.

preconditions.description: The fork branch that carries this contribution is named by the event key. Without it there is nothing to verify and the verifier reports unavailable rather than guessing.

The fork's forge is reachable and its pull request listing is readable. An unreachable forge is unavailable, never an implicit no-such-pull-request, because absence of evidence must not be read as evidence of absence.

permitted_actions: read the delivered contribution and the fork's pull request listing
dispatch a worker to carry the contribution onto a fork branch
open a pull request against the fork
read the fork pull request's own checks
write this loop's persistent state and execution record
forbidden_actions: merge any pull request, on the fork or anywhere else
close, reopen or edit a pull request this loop did not open
force-push, discard or tear down unlanded work
open or modify a pull request against the upstream repository
expand its own budget, authority or terminal set
treat a resolved-but-red check set as authorization to land

required_evidence: the fork pull request number observed on the forge for this branch
the pull request check summary, with passed, failed, pending and total counts
an explicit statement of whether the resolved check set is green

terminal_states.name: already_carried
terminal_states.description: The fork already carries this contribution and its checks are resolved. Reaching this must cost no model turn.

terminal_states.name: carried_and_checks_resolved
terminal_states.description: The contribution reached the fork as an open pull request and that pull request's checks finished running. This asserts the carry and nothing more: it does not assert the checks are green, and the failed count is recorded alongside it so the record can never be read as a green light. Whether the pull request may land is the merge decision, which this loop deliberately never makes.

terminal_states.name: needs_ruling
terminal_states.description: Whether this contribution should be carried at all cannot be settled from evidence and requires a captain ruling. The loop stops rather than guessing.

terminal_states.name: budget_exhausted
terminal_states.description: The iteration budget was spent before the carry could be verified. Exhaustion is a failure and is never reported as success.

terminal_states.name: verification_failed
terminal_states.description: The verifier ran and rejected the iteration, or could not establish the evidence at all. An unavailable verifier lands here and can never become a pass.

terminal_states.name: no_progress_stalled
terminal_states.description: Consecutive iterations produced no verifier-declared progress, so the loop stopped instead of repeating forever.

escalation.authority_owner: firstmate, escalating to the captain for the merge decision this loop never makes
escalation.channel: the task's durable status record, never a worker pane

idempotency.claim_scope: At most one open iteration per (spec id, fork branch). A repeated wake carrying an already-claimed branch is refused and mutates nothing, so noticing the same delivery twice cannot open two carries.

evidence.written_to: state/loopspec/executions.log, as one loop= record per execution

notes: This is the fleet's first production LoopSpec, authorized as the proof case on 2026-08-06. THE LOOP STOPS BEFORE THE MERGE, by design and not by omission: its terminal is a carried pull request whose checks have run, never a merged one. A loop that merged would prove the wrong thing and would quietly convert a delivery mechanism into an authority expansion. It is deliberately chosen for having a deterministic l2 verifier that needs no vendor diversity, bounded and reversible actions (a pull request can be closed), clear terminal states, and no authority expansion. capacity_stop_band_percent is 0 because the two-threshold capacity band ruled on 2026-08-03 is owned by a separate queued task; this spec does not reimplement a ruled-but-unimplemented contract, and the interpreter's stop-band enforcement remains exercised by the fixture suite.
